text: 信息茧房分自找的与强加的。
en: Information cocoons come in self-sought and imposed kinds.

text: 自找的代表就是抖淫系，“你关心的，才是头条”。
en: The self-sought kind is exemplified by the Douyin family: 'What you care about is the headline'.

text: 不同的年龄，不同的性别，不同的出身认知，他/她的抖淫，你去看看简直就是两个截然不同的世界。
en: Different ages, different genders, different backgrounds and cognitions — his/her Douyin, if you look at it, is simply two completely different worlds.

text: 举个最简单的日常的例子，后入时你眼中看到的与女人眼中看到的。
en: Take the simplest everyday example: during rear entry, what you see with your eyes versus what a woman sees with her eyes.

text: 你的视角是：
en: Your perspective is:

text: 而她的视角是：
en: And her perspective is:

text: 同一件事，你们都是完全不同的视角。
en: For the same matter, you both have completely different perspectives.

text: 老天天然的就给了你们不同的视角，就不想不能让你们看到的是一样的东西。
en: Heaven naturally gave you different perspectives — it simply doesn't want what you see to be the same thing.

text: 而强加的就是强尼懂得。
en: And the imposed kind is what Johnny understands.

text: 你问怎么避免？
en: You ask how to avoid it?

text: 不能。
en: You can't.

text: 美国人也不能。
en: Americans can't either.

text: 例如电视，美国人的电视频道是订阅的，你看一眼就是看一年。
en: Take television, for example: American TV channels are subscription-based — one look and you're watching for a year.

text: 而美国的电视系统是分民主党与共和党的。
en: And the American television system is divided between Democrats and Republicans.

text: 在传播媒体，民主党几乎居于绝对的统治（CNN），但是共和党有家fox。
en: In communication media, the Democrats are almost absolutely dominant (CNN), but the Republicans have a Fox.

text: 你订阅了民主党的电视系统，你基本就活在了民主党给你构造的世界里。
en: If you subscribe to the Democratic television system, you basically live in the world the Democrats constructed for you.

text: 那你说怎么办呢？
en: So what do you do?

text: 怎么避免人们只活在为自己构造的信息茧房呢？
en: How can we prevent people from living only in information cocoons constructed for themselves?

text: 答案是教育阶段的逻辑学教学。
en: The answer is logic teaching during the education stage.

text: 无法避免，但可提醒。
en: It cannot be avoided, but it can be warned against.

text: 美帝用的就是这个办法。
en: This is the method the American empire uses.

text: 也就是把“逻辑能力”这个能力事先就赋予你。
en: That is, the ability of 'logical ability' is given to you in advance.

text: 把“辩谎能力”这个能力事先先赋予你。
en: The ability of 'lie-detecting ability' is given to you in advance.

text: 先锻炼你的“辩谎”能力，再把你撒入一个撒谎社会。
en: First train your 'lie-detecting' ability, then throw you into a lying society.

text: 我们的祖宗也告诉过你的事情：
en: Our ancestors also told you things:

text: 远看成岭侧成峰，远近高低各不同。
en: Seen from afar, a range; from the side, a peak — different from far, near, high and low.

text: 还告诉了你：盲人摸象这个故事。
en: And they told you the story of blind men feeling an elephant.

text: 这就是告诉你，你看到的，即使是真的，也未必全面，甚至可以说，“一定不全面”。
en: This tells you that what you see, even if it is true, may not be comprehensive — indeed, it can be said to be 'certainly not comprehensive'.

text: 你看到的，基于你的能力、精力，以及别人想要你看到的，大概率的，只是事情的一个面。
en: What you see, based on your ability, energy, and what others want you to see, is most likely just one face of the matter.

text: 即使是真的，也只是事情的一个面。
en: Even if it is true, it is only one face of the matter.

text: 于是A坚信自己看到的世界是方的，B坚信自己看到的世界是圆的。
en: So A firmly believes the world he sees is square, and B firmly believes the world he sees is round.

text: AB各自都有无数的理由，觉得自己是真理，自己才是真理。
en: A and B each have countless reasons, feeling they are the truth, that they alone are the truth.

text: 觉得对方是错误的，应该把对方非人道消灭。
en: Feeling the other is wrong, and should be inhumanely eliminated.

text: 而逻辑学，则从根本上就告诉你，你们都对，但是都不全。
en: Logic, however, fundamentally tells you: you are both right, but neither is complete.

text: 因为，你们理解世界的工具，是语言。
en: Because the tool you use to understand the world is language.

text: 语言是你们进行思维的工具。
en: Language is the tool you use to think.

text: 也就是维特根斯坦的“语言即世界”“语言是我理解世界的边界”。
en: That is Wittgenstein's 'language is the world' and 'language is the boundary of my understanding of the world'.

text: 而语言只是真实的世界的一个投影。
en: And language is only a projection of the real world.

text: 语言是无法去表达与描述完全的真实的世界的，因为“不可说的东西，保持沉默”。
en: Language cannot express and describe the completely real world, because 'whereof one cannot speak, thereof one must be silent'.

text: 举的例子就是“鸡生蛋还是蛋生鸡”，这个经典的逻辑学问题。
en: The example given is 'the chicken or the egg', this classic logic question.

text: 而维特根斯坦的解读，就是真实的世界，就没有“鸡”这个东西，因为鸡是连贯的从恐龙一直延续到今天的一个动态物品，而只是你把其中的一个片段，命名叫做“鸡”。
en: And Wittgenstein's interpretation is that in the real world there is no such thing as a 'chicken', because a chicken is a dynamic thing continuing coherently from dinosaurs to today, and you merely name one fragment of it 'chicken'.

text: 所以，语言是不能直接、全面反馈真实与全面的世界的，语言只是为“达成共识”，而不是“认真、严谨、全面”的去表达世界。
en: So language cannot directly and comprehensively reflect the real and comprehensive world; language is only for 'reaching consensus', not for expressing the world 'seriously, rigorously and comprehensively'.

text: 所以，“不可说的东西，保持沉默”。
en: So, 'whereof one cannot speak, thereof one must be silent'.

text: 而维特根斯坦想要一种“理想语言”，就是这种语言“为唯一的一个事务取唯一的一个名字”“每一个词语都表示唯一的一个事务”。
en: And Wittgenstein wanted an 'ideal language', in which 'a unique name is given to a unique affair' and 'each word represents a unique affair'.

text: 这种语言会最大可能得接近真实世界。
en: This language would come as close as possible to the real world.

text: 但是不可能，因为语言具有自翻译、自进化、自演绎的功能。
en: But it is impossible, because language has the functions of self-translation, self-evolution and self-deduction.

text: 你不可能去创造一种“理想语言”，为每一个事务都取上唯一的名字，并每一个单词都代表唯一的一个事务。
en: You cannot create an 'ideal language' that gives a unique name to every affair, with every word representing a unique affair.

text: 例如，维特根斯坦举的例子，就是失业。
en: For example, Wittgenstein's example is unemployment.

text: 失业就是失业，对于失业这个唯一的事务，你就用唯一的词语失业来描述，而不要用“准备新的就业”“下岗”“待就业”“灵活就业”“待富人群”。
en: Unemployment is unemployment. For this unique affair of unemployment, you use the unique word unemployment to describe it, and do not use 'preparing for new employment', 'laid off', 'awaiting employment', 'flexible employment', 'people awaiting prosperity'.

text: 来表达。
en: To express it.

text: 例如征兵，这个唯一的事务，你就用唯一的词语去表达，你可以选择征兵，可以选择动员，但是在同一状态下，你应该用同一个词语去表达，例如一战二战，如果描述的是同一件事，你就应该用同一个词汇，例如西方通常用“mobilize”也就是动员、动员率来统一表达，而不能在一个事务上，一会用“踊跃参军”，一会用“拉丁抓夫”来表达。
en: For example, conscription: for this unique affair, you express it with a unique word. You can choose conscription, you can choose mobilisation, but in the same state, you should use the same word to express it. For example, World War I and World War II: if describing the same thing, you should use the same vocabulary — for example, the West usually uses 'mobilize', that is, mobilisation and mobilisation rate, to express it uniformly, and cannot, for one affair, at one moment use 'enthusiastic enlistment' and at another use 'press-ganging' to express it.

text: 例如，对乙酰氨基酚就是对乙酰氨基酚，你不能一会用对乙酰氨基酚，一会用感冒通、一会用感冒灵、一会用维C银翘片、一会用复方小儿退热栓来表达。
en: For example, paracetamol is paracetamol. You cannot at one moment use paracetamol, at another use Ganmaotong, at another Ganmaoling, at another Vitamin C Yinqiao Tablets, at another Compound Paediatric Antipyretic Suppositories to express it.

text: 例如，格列本脲就是格列本脲，你不能一会用格列本脲，一会用消渴丸来表达。
en: For example, glibenclamide is glibenclamide. You cannot at one moment use glibenclamide, at another use Xiaoke Pills to express it.

text: 例如，马来酸氯苯那敏就是马来酸氯苯那敏，你不能一会用马来酸氯苯那敏，一会用咳特灵来表达。
en: For example, chlorphenamine maleate is chlorphenamine maleate. You cannot at one moment use chlorphenamine maleate, at another use Ke Te Ling to express it.

text: 例如，蝙蝠shi就是蝙蝠shi，你不能一会用蝙蝠shi，一会用夜明砂来表达。
en: For example, bat shit is bat shit. You cannot at one moment use bat shit, at another use Night-Shining Sand to express it.

text: 例如，老鼠shi就是老鼠shi，你不能一会用老鼠shi，一会用五灵脂来表达。
en: For example, rat shit is rat shit. You cannot at one moment use rat shit, at another use Five Spirits Fat to express it.

text: 例如，猫咪shi就是猫咪shi，你不能一会用猫咪shi，一会用月明砂来表达。
en: For example, cat shit is cat shit. You cannot at one moment use cat shit, at another use Moon-Bright Sand to express it.

text: 例如，农村旱厕就是农村旱厕，你不能一会用农村旱厕，一会用人中黄来表达。
en: For example, a rural dry toilet is a rural dry toilet. You cannot at one moment use rural dry toilet, at another use Ren Zhong Huang to express it.

text: 例如，qu就是qu，你不能一会用qu，一会用水仙子来表达。
en: For example, maggots are maggots. You cannot at one moment use maggots, at another use Water Fairies to express it.

text: 避免信息茧房的办法就是逻辑学。
en: The way to avoid information cocoons is logic.

text: 所以国内出版的维特根斯坦哲学论，封面是个梯子。
en: So the domestically published Wittgenstein's Tractatus has a ladder on its cover.

text: 就是让你出坑的。
en: It is to let you climb out of the pit.

text: 所以，1930年代开始，苏联全苏禁止了逻辑学教学。
en: So, starting in the 1930s, the Soviet Union banned logic teaching across the whole union.

text: “信息茧房”是一个比喻，指的是人们在互联网上只接触到与自己现有观点和兴趣相一致的信息，从而限制了视野和思想的多样性。
en: 'Information cocoon' is a metaphor referring to people only coming into contact on the internet with information consistent with their existing views and interests, thereby limiting the diversity of their horizons and thoughts.

text: 要突破信息茧房，可以尝试以下方法：
en: To break through information cocoons, you can try the following methods:

text: 1. 多元化信息源：主动寻找和订阅不同观点和领域的信息来源，包括新闻网站、博客、社交媒体账号等
en: 1. Diversify information sources: actively seek and subscribe to information sources with different views and fields, including news websites, blogs, social media accounts, etc.

text: 2. 批判性思维：培养批判性思维能力，对接触到的信息进行分析和质疑，而不是被动接受。
en: 2. Critical thinking: cultivate critical thinking ability, analyse and question the information you come into contact with, rather than passively accepting it.

text: 3. 跨领域学习：定期学习新的领域或话题，这有助于拓宽知识面和理解不同的观点。
en: 3. Cross-field learning: regularly learn new fields or topics, which helps broaden your knowledge and understand different views.

text: 4. 使用推荐系统：利用社交媒体和新闻平台的推荐系统探索不熟悉的主题和观点。
en: 4. Use recommendation systems: use social media and news platform recommendation systems to explore unfamiliar topics and views.

text: 5. 社交媒体设置：调整社交媒体算法偏好，减少过滤泡泡效应，即算法根据用户历史行为推荐相似内容的倾向。
en: 5. Social media settings: adjust social media algorithm preferences to reduce the filter bubble effect, i.e., the tendency of algorithms to recommend similar content based on user history.

text: 6. 讨论和辩论：与持有不同观点的人进行讨论和辩论，这有助于理解多样性并促进个人成长。
en: 6. Discussion and debate: discuss and debate with people holding different views, which helps understand diversity and promote personal growth.

text: 7. 阅读书：阅读不同类型和主题的书籍，尤其是那些挑战你现有观点的书籍。
en: 7. Reading books: read books of different types and topics, especially those that challenge your existing views.

text: 8. 多语言内容：尝试阅读或观看不同语言的内容，这有助于了解不同文化和视
en: 8. Multilingual content: try reading or watching content in different languages, which helps understand different cultures and perspectives.

text: 9. 避免快速判断：在形成观点之前，给予自己充分的时间来考虑和评估信息。
en: 9. Avoid quick judgments: before forming a view, give yourself sufficient time to consider and evaluate information.

text: 10. 开放态度：保持开放的心态，愿意接受新的想法和观点，即使它们与你的现有信念相冲突。
en: 10. Open attitude: keep an open mind, willing to accept new ideas and views, even if they conflict with your existing beliefs.

text: 11. 定期反思：定期反思自己的信息消费习惯和信念，看看是否有偏差或局限性。
en: 11. Regular reflection: regularly reflect on your information consumption habits and beliefs, to see if there are biases or limitations.

text: 12. 使用工具：利用一些工具和浏览器插件来打破过滤泡泡，比如推荐系统调节工具。
en: 12. Use tools: use some tools and browser plugins to break filter bubbles, such as recommendation system adjustment tools.

text: 13. 参与线下活动：参加社区活动、讲座、研讨会等，与不同背景的人面对面交流。
en: 13. Participate in offline activities: attend community activities, lectures, seminars, etc., and communicate face-to-face with people from different backgrounds.

text: 14.教育自己：通过正规教育途径，如参加课程或研讨会，系统地学习新知识。
en: 14. Educate yourself: through formal education channels, such as attending courses or seminars, systematically learn new knowledge.

text: 15. 自我挑战：故意将自己置于不舒服的环境中，比如阅读对立观点的文章或观看辩论，以促进个人成长。
en: 15. Self-challenge: deliberately place yourself in uncomfortable environments, such as reading articles with opposing views or watching debates, to promote personal growth.

text: 通过这些方法，可以逐步打破信息茧房，促进个人的全面发展和思想的多元化。
en: Through these methods, you can gradually break information cocoons, promoting comprehensive personal development and diversity of thought.
